Terra confirmed or left unresolved a deterministic risk gate.

findingIds: The packet identifies 50 affected baseline items. All 107 baseline rows were reconciled: 58 exact_match/accurately_unavailable, 22 variant_match/accurately_unavailable, and 27 missing_from_source/accurately_unavailable; there were 107 unique reconciled keys and no duplicate reconciled keys.

The current Wharf page and June 17, 2026 restaurant-issued PDF enumerate products absent from or materially different from the frozen catalog, including enoki mushroom, taco teaser, cotija corn dip, chicken + black bean, fruit bowl, current drinks, and takeout-pack presentations.
The frozen catalog contains removed or renamed products and duplicate rice-bowl presentations, so the baseline is not an exact representation of the current menu.

The official nutrition page describes an allergen-filtering workflow but does not expose a complete static item-level matrix. It cannot independently support complete allergen arrays, negatives, or item-specific may-contain conclusions.
The current PDF provides a global instruction to ask about potential allergen cross-contamination. This supports a global caution only, not item-level may-contain arrays or item-level clearance.

Restaurant-issued explicit positives remain valid when narrowly scoped. Examples include gluten labels, pistachio labels, named shrimp or fish identities, cotija and other named cheeses, sesame-soy descriptions, and gluten-bearing named preparations. These positives do not imply complete allergen arrays.

Rejected any interpretation of Luna's currentProductCount=0, currentOnlyCount=0, and baselineOnlyCount=0 as a complete catalog reconciliation; the primary sources enumerate a substantial current catalog.
Rejected the deterministic nonExactItemCount=107 as internally inconsistent with the packet's reconciliation summary, which reports 58 exact matches. The underlying drift remains confirmed.
Rejected treating crossContactCount=2 as two supported item-level cross-contact findings. The strongest current source supplies only global cross-contamination language.

Rejected any blanket erasure of baseline positives merely because the current allergen interface is incomplete. Explicit restaurant-issued ingredients and unavoidable named identities can still support narrow positive evidence.
Rejected culinary assumptions that promote descriptive ingredients into unstated allergens, negatives, complete arrays, or cross-contact conclusions.
